<h1 id="16S-Pipeline-Validation-%E2%80%94-wetSpring">16S Pipeline Validation — wetSpring<a class="anchor-link" href="#16S-Pipeline-Validation-%E2%80%94-wetSpring">¶</a></h1><p>The complete 16S metagenomics pipeline — FASTQ parsing, quality filtering,
dereplication, DADA2 denoising, chimera detection, taxonomy classification,
diversity calculation, and UniFrac — implemented in sovereign Rust with
<strong>1 runtime dependency</strong> (flate2 for gzip).</p>
<p>This notebook loads frozen validation results from wetSpring experiments
and visualizes the evidence that the Rust pipeline matches the established
Galaxy/QIIME2/Python pipeline at machine-epsilon precision.</p>
<p><strong>Data sources</strong>: <code>experiments/results/</code> (frozen JSON artifacts)</p>
<p><strong>Reproduce</strong>: Run any validation binary with <code>cargo run --release --bin &lt;name&gt;</code>
in the wetSpring repository. See <a href="https://primals.eco/lab/reproduce/">primals.eco/lab/reproduce</a>.</p>
<hr/>
<p><em>For other springs: adapt this pattern by loading your own <code>experiments/results/</code> JSONs.
The cell structure (load → parse → visualize → provenance) is the template.</em></p>

<div class="cell border-box-sizing text_cell rendered"><div class="inner_cell">
<div class="text_cell_render border-box-sizing rendered_html">
<h2 id="The-Pipeline">The Pipeline<a class="anchor-link" href="#The-Pipeline">¶</a></h2><pre><code>Raw FASTQ (NCBI SRA)          ← real data, not simulated
    │
    ├─ Parse (sovereign FASTQ parser)
    ├─ Quality filter (Q≥20, length≥200)
    ├─ Merge paired-end reads
    ├─ Dereplicate (unique sequences)
    ├─ DADA2 denoise (error model → ASVs)
    ├─ Chimera detection (de novo + reference)
    ├─ Taxonomy (Naïve Bayes, SILVA 138.2)
    ├─ Diversity (Shannon, Simpson, Chao1, UniFrac)
    └─ PCoA ordination
</code></pre>
<p>Every step has a Python/R baseline. Every step has a Rust implementation.
Parity is checked at machine epsilon (1e-15 for f64).</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
